description: Selected benchmark catalog for CompetencyGaps benchmark search.
notes: This catalog contains benchmark metadata, not evaluation examples or SAE profiles.
AfriMMLU and AfriMGSM are separate entries from the combined selection.
Hugging Face selected IDs are preserved alongside their current canonical IDs.
Split values are row counts. Configurations and translations can overlap; do not sum them as independent examples.
Revision SHAs come from Hub metadata. Viewer/card counts were checked separately and are not download-verified at those revisions.
A null license or an empty language list means the inspected source did not declare that metadata.
Licenses are repository/card declarations; task-specific exceptions are recorded in entry notes.
Dataset loading and evaluation execution have not been tested.

benchmarks.name: IFEval
benchmarks.description: Instruction-following evaluation prompts with constraints that can be checked by heuristics.
notes: The evaluation prompts are stored in the train split (541 rows); the split name does not imply a recommended training use.

benchmarks.name: WildBench
benchmarks.description: Challenging real-user LLM tasks drawn from WildChat, with evaluation checklists.
notes: The card recommends config v2, split test. Keep v1-legacy, v2, and v2-hard distinct; v2-hard is a 256-row subset.
The YAML dataset_info includes a stale default entry; current card configs and viewer list v1-legacy, v2, and v2-hard.
The card links CC BY 4.0 in its prose despite having no license key in YAML.

benchmarks.name: BIG-bench Hard
benchmarks.description: BIG-bench Hard tasks exposed as separate dataset configurations.
notes: There are 27 task configurations, all with a test split; explicitly select a task or declare how tasks will be combined.
Most task test splits contain 250 rows; causal_judgement has 187, penguins_in_a_table 146, and snarks 178.
This HF card does not declare a license or language, so these fields remain unknown.

benchmarks.name: MuSR
benchmarks.description: Multistep soft reasoning benchmark covering murder mysteries, object placements, and team allocation.
notes: This HF repository has one default configuration and task-named splits, not three task configurations: murder_mysteries (250), object_placements (256), team_allocation (250).
Explicitly choose one task split or declare a cross-task combination.

benchmarks.name: HellaSwag
benchmarks.description: Commonsense natural-language inference benchmark for choosing a plausible continuation.
notes: One default configuration has train, validation, and test splits; select the intended evaluation split explicitly.
MIT is stated in the card licensing section although YAML omits a license key. English is confirmed by the card language metadata.

benchmarks.name: AI2 ARC
benchmarks.description: Multiple-choice grade-school science questions divided into ARC-Challenge and ARC-Easy.
notes: ARC-Challenge and ARC-Easy are separate configurations; do not collapse them into an unspecified ARC default.
Counts cover the question-answering benchmark splits, not the additional science sentence corpus mentioned in the card.

benchmarks.name: MMLU-Pro
benchmarks.description: Challenging multidisciplinary multiple-choice questions with expanded answer options.
notes: Test and validation are distinct splits; freeze the dataset revision because the card records question/option corrections.
MMLU ancestry alone does not establish redundancy with an existing MMLU suite.

benchmarks.name: TruthfulQA
benchmarks.description: Questions designed to elicit false answers associated with common human misconceptions.
notes: Choose generation or multiple_choice explicitly; their 817-row validation splits represent different task formats of the same benchmark, not 1,634 independent questions.
The card reports 38 topic categories.

benchmarks.name: LegalBench
benchmarks.description: A collection of English legal-reasoning tasks with task-specific schemas and small few-shot training splits.
notes: The card describes 162 tasks; configuration metadata below records the currently verified repository/viewer contents.
Select task configurations explicitly; the card marks abercrombie as default, so a default configuration does not represent the entire benchmark.
The repository card declares cc-by-4.0, but its licensing section states that LegalBench tasks have different licenses; consult per-task sources/paper before reuse.
The card calls train splits few-shot labeled examples; test is the evaluation split name exposed by the Viewer API.

benchmarks.name: MedQA (USMLE, four options)
benchmarks.description: English medical-exam multiple-choice question answering in a four-option dataset variant.
notes: Use the test split for evaluation; 1,273 is its verified row count, not the whole repository total.
The repository card is brief and links the original MedQA paper; no additional configuration or validation split is assumed.

benchmarks.name: HumanEval
benchmarks.description: Handwritten Python function-completion problems with docstrings, canonical solutions, and unit tests.
notes: The verified configuration is openai_humaneval, not default.
The card confirms Python programs with English natural-language comments/docstrings; the declared natural-language metadata is en.
Only test is exposed; profiling inputs does not execute generated code or establish functional correctness.

benchmarks.name: Mostly Basic Python Problems (MBPP)
benchmarks.description: Crowd-sourced entry-level Python programming tasks with code solutions and automated test cases.
notes: Choose full or sanitized explicitly; sanitized is a hand-verified/revised subset, not an independent benchmark.
The full configuration has 974 rows across all splits; test has 500. Sanitized has 427 rows across all splits; test has 257.
Use validation, the actual metadata split name; the README prose also uses evaluation, and its older loading snippet describes totals as test counts.
The prompt split is intended for few-shot prompting, not evaluation or training.

benchmarks.name: XSTest
benchmarks.description: Contrast prompts for measuring exaggerated safety behavior.
notes: Auto-gated repository. Unauthenticated card-file and Viewer-size requests returned HTTP 401; counts above are from public repository card metadata.
No access acceptance or authenticated loading was attempted.
Card names the logical split test (450 rows), although its data file is named data/train-00000-of-00001.parquet.

benchmarks.name: HarmBench
benchmarks.description: Behavior prompts from HarmBench for automated red teaming and robust refusal evaluation.
notes: Auto-gated repository. Unauthenticated card-file and Viewer-size requests returned HTTP 401; counts above are from public repository card metadata.
No access acceptance or authenticated loading was attempted.
Choose contextual, copyright, or standard explicitly. These are behavior prompts; this mirror does not establish a full HarmBench evaluation pipeline.

benchmarks.name: Anthropic Model-Written Evaluations
benchmarks.description: Model-authored evaluation collections for persona, sycophancy, advanced AI risks, and gender bias.
notes: Repository collections are persona/, sycophancy/, advanced-ai-risk/, and winogenerated/. Viewer reports default/train with 3252 rows; this is not treated as the count of all collection files. A collection/file manifest must be chosen before evaluation.

benchmarks.name: Global-MMLU
benchmarks.description: Translations of MMLU across 42 languages, with cultural-sensitivity annotations on a subset.
notes: Selected ID is retained; Hugging Face resolves it to CohereLabs/Global-MMLU. This is a repository alias, not a new selection.
42 language configurations; each has dev 285 and test 14042 rows. The Lite dataset is a separate repository and is not selected.
Choose language and, if needed, culturally sensitive/agnostic annotation filters explicitly; no language or filtered subset is selected here.

benchmarks.name: AfriMMLU
benchmarks.description: Translations of an MMLU subset into African languages, with English and French reference subsets.
notes: Selected ID is valid. Viewer verifies 18 configurations; card prose says 17 languages, so its narrative count differs from current metadata.
Use three-letter configuration codes (for example eng, kin, swa), not the mixed two/three-letter card language tags. Each configuration has validation 83, dev 25, and test 500 rows.

benchmarks.name: AfriMGSM
benchmarks.description: Translations of a GSM8K subset for grade-school mathematics evaluation in African languages.
notes: Selected ID is valid. Viewer verifies 19 configurations; card prose says 18 languages, and its displayed count table omits some configurations.
Use three-letter configuration codes (for example eng, kin, swa). Each configuration has train 8 and test 250 rows; train is mapped to data/<code>/dev.tsv in card configuration metadata.

benchmarks.name: LongBench
benchmarks.description: Bilingual long-context tasks covering QA, summarization, few-shot learning, synthetic tasks, and code completion.
notes: Selected ID is retained; Hugging Face resolves it to zai-org/LongBench. This is a repository alias, not a new selection.
Canonical Viewer /splits and /size return HTTP 500: Dataset scripts are no longer supported, but found LongBench.py. The legacy card load_dataset example is not verified as working.
34 declared test configurations: 21 base LongBench and 13 LongBench-E (_e). Counts are card-reported task statistics, not verification by downloading rows. Choose tasks and base/E variant explicitly.
Dataset license is unknown: no card license is declared. The Apache 2.0 header on LongBench.py is a code license and is not treated as the data license.
